lineage.summary: Initial version of the LIN Specification; heavily influenced by the VLITE bus used by some automotive companies.
Mainly physical-layer changes, targeting improved compatibility between nodes.

Major Revision Step. Spec completely reworked. Standardised configuration/diagnostics and Node Capability files. Introduced enhanced checksum + reconfiguration + diagnostics + automatic baud-rate detection + response_error status monitoring.
Clarifications, configuration modified, transport layer enhanced, diagnostics added.
Updated document according to LIN 2.1 Errata sheet 1.4. Softened bit sampling specification.
Corrected wake-up signal definition in chapter 2.6.2 (current revision).

backward_compat_traps.lin_1_x_behaviour: All frames use classic checksum (over data bytes only).
backward_compat_traps.lin_2_x_behaviour: Non-diagnostic frames use enhanced checksum (over PID + data bytes); diagnostic frames (IDs 0x3C / 0x3D) still use classic.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A LIN 2.x slave node cannot operate with a LIN 1.3 master because the LIN 1.3 master cannot produce enhanced checksum. A LIN 2.x master driving a mixed cluster must know which slaves are LIN 1.3 (use classic) vs LIN 2.x (use enhanced) on a per-frame-ID basis.

backward_compat_traps.lin_2_2_behaviour: Softened bit sampling specification (per revision history).
backward_compat_traps.trap: A LIN 2.1 compliance test may reject a LIN 2.2-tuned implementation as too lenient; do not retrofit a softened-sample slave into a strict-2.1 cluster without a tolerance audit.

backward_compat_traps.lin_2_2A_behaviour: Corrected wake-up signal definition in chapter 2.6.2.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A 2.2 implementation may have a slightly different wake-up signal interpretation than a 2.2A implementation; verify against the 2.2A text before claiming 2.2A compliance.

backward_compat_traps.lin_2_x_behaviour: IDs 0x3E and 0x3F are reserved for future LIN extended format and shall not be used in a LIN 2.x cluster.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Some legacy nodes may have used 0x3E / 0x3F as private signal carriers; this is non-compliant in LIN 2.x and will collide with any future extended-format LIN implementation.

backward_compat_traps.lin_2_2_behaviour: LIN 2.2 physical layer is backwards compatible with LIN 1.3 — but not the other way around. LIN 2.2 sets harder requirements.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A node implemented to LIN 2.2 physical layer can join a LIN 1.3 cluster, but a LIN 1.3 node may fail EMC/voltage thresholds when placed in a LIN 2.2 cluster.

fields.version_naming_history_note: The LIN Consortium released seven revisions (1.0 → 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.3 → 2.0 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.2A) between 1999 and 2010. LIN 2.0 was the major revision step that standardised diagnostics, configuration, and the Node Capability File workflow. LIN 2.2A is the final revision before the LIN protocol was harmonised into ISO 17987 (2016+).
